To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

aldrin under nontolerated condition, administered either a single dose or for 12 days, enhanced locomotion activity of rats and the increase in locomotion activity was greater in rats administered aldrin for twelve consecutive days than that caused by single day aldrin treatment.
aldrin under nontolerate condition enhances locomotor activity by inhibiting the GABAergic system and activating dopaminergic and cholinergic systems.
aldrin-induced locomotor activity is due to the inhibition of GABAergic activity along with stimulation of dopaminergic activity by inhibition of cholinergics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible involvement of central GABA-cholinergic-dopa-minergic interaction in aldrin-induced LA.
the possible involvement of the GABAergic-cholingeric-dopaminergic interactions in aldrin-induced LA in rats.
the possible interaction of central GABA, choline and dopamine system in the regulation of aldrin-induced LA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aldrin-induced locomotor activity, under nontolerance, is regulated by the central GABA/cholinergic-dopamine interaction.
the central GABA-choline-dopamine interaction plays an important role in the regulation of aldrin-induced LA.
aldrin under nontolerated condition increases central cholinergic and GABAergic activity, which may be due to the activation of central dopaminergic system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aldrin increases central dopaminergic activity via inhibition of central cholinergic activity, which in turn, decreases central GABAergic system.
aldrin-induced locomotor activity is mediated via the GABAergic-cholingeric-dopaminergic interrelationship in the central nervous system.
aldrin increases LA of rats under nontolerated conditions and the effect may be mediated via a possible interaction of central cholinergic, GABAergic and dopamineric systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chronic aldrin administration may cause greater neurotoxicity than acute exposure.
the GABAergic, dopaminergic and cholinergic systems are interconnected in the regulation of motor behavior.
the central GABA-DA-AC interaction plays a crucial role in the aldrin-induced LA.
